SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: 2–3-day history of increased shortness of breath, wheeze, and cough (dry) noted initially while running; persists with brisk walking. Salbutamol (“blue inhaler”) provides little relief.
- Symptom details:
  • Onset: 2–3 days ago.  
  • Progression: Persistent; using reliever inhaler daily, morning and evening, and PRN.  
  • Sputum: None.  
  • No hospital admissions for asthma; last acute attack 3–4 years ago (managed with inhalers only; no oral steroids/antibiotics).  
  • Last asthma review: ≈2 years ago.  
  • Peak flow when well: ~380 L/min (patient-reported); no recent reading.
- Past medical history: Asthma. Possible eczema (self-reported, not formally diagnosed). Hay fever.
- Medications:  
  • Salbutamol inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented (patient using PRN and twice daily prophylactically).  
  • Beclomethasone (Clenil) inhaler – 3 puffs BID (per discussion).  
  • Cetraben – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  • Hydrocortisone topical – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  • “Flanel Bactroban” (name unclear) – dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.
- Social history: Not discussed.

Objective:
- Tele-consultation; no in-person examination performed.
- No current vitals recorded.
- Historical peak flow when well: ~380 L/min (patient-reported).
- No investigations performed during call.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute asthma exacerbation
   - Assessment: Likely mild asthma exacerbation.
   - Investigations planned: Face-to-face GP review with chest examination and peak-flow measurement; further tests (e.g., spirometry, pulse oximetry) as indicated.
   - Treatment planned:  
     • Increase beclomethasone (Clenil) to 4 puffs BID until reviewed.  
     • Continue salbutamol inhaler up to every 2 hours PRN.  
     • Educated on red-flag signs; advised to attend A&E if breathlessness worsens or requirement for salbutamol becomes frequent (≈every 2 hours) before review.
   - Relevant referrals: Arrange urgent GP appointment within next few days.

2. Asthma follow-up / routine monitoring
   - Assessment: Asthma management review overdue (last review 2 years ago).
   - Investigations planned: Formal asthma review with nurse/GP; peak-flow diary; consider inhaler technique check and action plan update.
   - Treatment planned: To be determined after review.

Quality checks:

• Missing expected elements: Current vitals, smoking status, alcohol intake, complete medication reconciliation with doses, allergy confirmation (beyond drugs), detailed social history.  
• Internal conflicts: None noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear overall; 1–2 drug names indistinct (“Flanel Bactroban” unclear).
